text: Stopwatch shall report how far the tablet's recorded waits differ from waits timed by a person, as a mean difference in minutes with a 95% interval.
acceptance: All children verified.
rationale: Four clinic sessions agreed the records cannot separate 'measured differently' from 'really slower'. Only a measurement beside the tablet can.

text: The des model shall reproduce the clinic's tablet-era day closely enough to size the study.
acceptance: All children verified.
rationale: The study's length and its blind spots are queueing effects; they have to be simulated before anyone spends a morning on them.

text: Simulated arrivals shall average between 7.2 and 7.9 per day over 10000 seeded days.
acceptance: T-SIM-RATE passes: mean arrivals per day in [7.2, 7.9]; the tablet era had 113 visits in 15 days (7.53).
rationale: Rate fixes how many patients one observer can time.

text: Simulated true waits shall have quartiles within 3 minutes of 23, 34 and 45.
acceptance: T-SIM-WAIT passes over 10000 seeded days.
rationale: Tablet-era quartiles from visits.csv (clinic-eras.mjs). Until the study runs, the recorded waits are the only shape we have.

text: The tablet error model shall apply a set offset, jitter, minute rounding and dropped entries, and with all four at zero shall record every true time exactly.
acceptance: T-SIM-ERR-ZERO passes (recorded equals true for every patient in 1000 days) and T-SIM-ERR-EACH passes (each component alone moves the recorded mean by its set amount within 0.2 min).
rationale: The hypotheses being tested have to exist in the model, or the power figures are about nothing.

text: Two runs with the same seed and parameters shall produce byte-identical event traces.
acceptance: T-SIM-DET passes.
rationale: A sizing nobody can reproduce is an anecdote.

text: The controller shall decide which patients the observer times and when the study stops.
acceptance: All children verified.
rationale: Left to choose, an observer times the patients who are convenient; those are the quiet hours.

text: The controller shall select patients by a seeded draw at sign-in, and shall record a selected patient it cannot time as missed rather than substitute another.
acceptance: T-CTL-PICK passes: every selection in the log is reproducible from the seed and the sign-in sequence, and no unselected patient is ever timed.
rationale: Substitution is how selection bias gets in.

text: Over a simulated study, the share of timed patients from each clinic hour shall be within 10 percentage points of that hour's share of arrivals.
acceptance: T-CTL-COVER passes over 1000 simulated studies at the default parameters.
rationale: Timing whoever comes next while free misses 37% of arrivals, and they are the ones who arrive while someone is already waiting (modulo-sizing.mjs).

text: The controller shall run stage 1 to exactly 6 timed patients with no early stop. It shall run stage 2, to 12 timed patients cumulative, if and only if the stage-1 interval contains both 0 and 15 minutes. No one may start or skip stage 2 by any other rule. The per-stage alpha shall be fixed in this file, from A-PWR-FALSE on the full controller, before the first tap.
acceptance: T-CTL-STOP passes on scripted sequences that stop at stage 1 by excluding 0, stop at stage 1 by excluding 15, go to stage 2 only when both are inside the interval, and never stop before 6.
rationale: Stopping is decided before the data, not after looking at it. Draft trigger, council round 2. Morphyx's trigger (stage 2 iff stage 1 fails to reject 0) runs stage 2 in 97% of studies when the tablet is honest, about 5 mornings in total, to answer a 5-minute question the clinic hasn't asked. This trigger runs it in 0.2% (SD 5) to 31% (SD 10) of studies, whatever the truth is.

text: The controller code shall make identical decisions under run() with a simulated observer and under runRealtime() with a fake clock fed the same signals.
acceptance: T-CTL-SAME passes: decision logs compared entry by entry, same sim times.
rationale: The controller that was sized must be the one that runs.

text: Every observer tap and every controller decision shall be written to an append-only log from which the session can be replayed.
acceptance: T-CTL-REPLAY passes: replaying a recorded log reproduces the decision log exactly.
rationale: If the result is disputed, the log is the evidence.

text: The study design shall detect the error that would explain the tablet-era jump.
acceptance: All children verified.
rationale: The design should be able to answer the question it is asked.

text: With a tablet offset of 15 minutes and jitter SD of 10 minutes, simulated studies shall reject zero offset in at least 95% of runs.
acceptance: A-PWR-DETECT: at least 0.95 over 5000 seeded studies run through the controller. Tracked as TPM-POWER (min, threshold 0.95).
rationale: The clinic's question is whether the whole 17 -> 34 jump is the instrument, which means a 15-minute offset. A scratch sim of the two-stage rule at alpha 0.0294 per stage gives 0.986. The 5-minute question gets power 0.41 under this rule; it is a separate, later ask, not part of this study.

text: With zero offset, simulated studies shall reject zero offset in at most 6% of runs.
acceptance: A-PWR-FALSE: at most 0.06 over 5000 seeded studies. Tracked as TPM-FALSE-ALARM (max, threshold 0.06).
rationale: Optional stopping inflates false alarms; this measures by how much.

text: At the default parameters, 80% of simulated studies shall stop within 4 sessions.
acceptance: A-PWR-LENGTH: the 80th percentile of sessions to stop is at most 4. Tracked as TPM-SESSIONS (max, threshold 4, objective 3).
rationale: A manager's mornings are the real budget. One observer times 2.4 patients a morning (modulo-sizing.mjs), so 6 timed is about 2.5 mornings and 12 is about 5. The clinic is asked for two, with up to three more written into the same letter.

text: The study shall be run at the clinic.
acceptance: All children verified.
rationale: Nothing in the lab can verify these. vv will show them unverified until the clinic does them, and they hold back their share of earned value.

text: At the start and end of each session the observer shall record the tablet clock against the observer's device clock, and the session shall be discarded if they differ by more than 30 seconds.
acceptance: D-REAL-CLOCK: both readings present in every session log and every kept session within 30 seconds.
rationale: A clock offset would look like a recording offset. This was one of the clinic's three agreed checks.

text: The clinic shall complete one study under the controller and the report shall state the mean difference with its 95% interval.
acceptance: D-REAL-STUDY: a completed log at the clinic, replayed through the report, giving the interval.
rationale: The point of the whole thing.

text: The vendor's written answer on what triggers 'signed in' and 'seen' shall be filed with the study.
acceptance: I-REAL-VENDOR: the answer is in the study folder, dated.
rationale: The offset says how big the difference is; the vendor says why.

text: A patient who declines to be timed shall be recorded as declined and not timed.
acceptance: I-REAL-DECLINE: the session sheet has a decline field and the controller treats declined like missed.
rationale: Being timed is the patient's choice, and declines count against coverage, so they have to be counted, not hidden.
